heading: Isolation
body: `YON_ISOLATION=warm` is the default, because Tachyon is serverless-first. Tachyon keeps a controller's process running after its first request and sends it later requests for the same controller, one at a time. `YON_WARM_MAX_REQUESTS` (default 1000) and `YON_WARM_IDLE_SECONDS` (default 60) bound how long one process lives. `YON_ISOLATION=process` runs a new child process for each request instead, for always-on servers that want a clean process every time. `YON_ISOLATION=firecracker` gives each request to a control program for microVMs (small virtual machines). `YON_FIRECRACKER_DRIVER`, `POOL`, `VCPUS`, `MEMORY_MIB` and `EGRESS` configure it. Tachyon reads this setting from the environment, not from a config file. The reason is that the right isolation depends on where a deployment runs, not on the source code. Firecracker mode supports only JavaScript and Python controllers. A controller in another language, TypeScript included, fails with `TY2010` before the driver starts, so it needs warm or process mode. For supported languages, the handler protocol and the build do not change. If the policy is invalid or only half declared, for example a warm setting with another mode, it fails with TY2010 before any route runs. On Windows, `YON_ISOLATION=firecracker` fails with `TY2010` when the server starts, because Firecracker needs a Linux host with KVM and Tachyon cannot check the driver's file permissions there.
